mcqs.q: What did the study identify as a key reason people do not seek pet support when eligible?
o: Fear of being judged, stigma, guilt and shame
Believing the pet was not really ill
mcqs.e: Findings centered on fear of judgment, disclosure, stigma, guilt, shame, lack of awareness, financial concerns, and wanting to manage independently.

mcqs.q: Which three broader ideological narratives underpinned participants' stories?
mcqs.e: The authors identified 'giving back,' 'equity,' and 'sacrifice' as the underpinning narratives.

mcqs.q: What was the authors' main recommendation to charities?
o: Reframe how support is advertised and delivered to counteract these influences
Require proof of income before help
mcqs.e: They argued support must be reframed to explicitly counteract stigma-related influences to ensure animals get needed care.

mcqs.q: How did veterinary students generally describe their experience on the remote Indigenous community rotations?
o: Welcomed and well supported by communities and the team
mcqs.e: Participants reported feeling welcomed and supported by the communities and connected to the veterinary team.

mcqs.q: Which factors did the study highlight as important for supporting students on community-based rotations?
o: Building community relationships, the right team, and debriefing during downtime
mcqs.e: The study emphasized building relationships, picking the right team, and implementing debriefing and decompressing activities.

mcqs.q: What was more important to volunteer satisfaction in this study?
o: Internal shelter factors rather than individual volunteer traits
mcqs.e: Internal shelter factors mattered more to satisfaction than the traits of the individual volunteer.

mcqs.q: Volunteers reported greater satisfaction with their experience and voice when volunteering at what kind of shelter?
o: Limited-intake shelters with higher save rates
mcqs.e: Satisfaction with voice and the experience was higher at limited-intake shelters with higher save rates.

mcqs.q: How did opportunities for 'voice' relate to overall satisfaction?
o: Volunteers more negative about voice were significantly less satisfied
Voice only mattered for new volunteers
mcqs.e: Volunteers more negative about their opportunities for voice were significantly less satisfied overall.

mcqs.q: What best distinguished different dog breeds in this hair analysis?
mcqs.e: Microscopic features distinguished breeds, whereas micro-metric values showed no remarkable distinctions.

mcqs.q: What did the study conclude about micro-metric measurement values across breeds?
o: They did not show remarkable distinctions
mcqs.e: The authors found micro-metric values did not show remarkable distinctions between breeds.

mcqs.q: A rare 'split end' condition was observed in which breed?
mcqs.e: The rare split-end condition was seen in the Dachshund breed.

mcqs.q: A satisfactory body condition score in these Hong Kong shelter cats was associated with which practices?
o: Regular veterinary input, frequent disinfection, and frequent water changes
mcqs.e: Satisfactory BCS was associated with regular vet input, more than once daily disinfection, and more than once daily water change.

mcqs.q: Oculo-nasal discharge (a marker of upper respiratory infection) was associated with what?
o: Lack of regular veterinary input and infrequent water changes
mcqs.e: URI signs were linked to lack of regular vet input and less frequent water changes.

mcqs.q: A dull coat was associated with which single factor?
mcqs.e: Lack of regular feeding was the only factor associated with a dull coat.

mcqs.q: What was the study's overall conclusion about 'cuteness' (baby schema) and length of stay?
o: Cuteness strongly shortened length of stay
Cuteness may not be as influential on length of stay as hypothesized
Only coat color predicted length of stay
mcqs.e: The study found cuteness may not be as influential on cats' length of stay as had been hypothesized.

mcqs.q: Which variable was found to influence length of stay in the analysis?
mcqs.e: Subjective cuteness in survey 1 was the only variable of influence on length of stay.

mcqs.q: What were the estimated outcomes for cats entering Australian pounds, shelters, and rescues in 2018–2019?
mcqs.e: The study estimated about 5% reclaimed, 65% rehomed, and 28% euthanized.

mcqs.q: How did euthanasia rates at council-run pounds compare with animal welfare organizations?
o: Council-run pounds had nearly double the euthanasia rate
mcqs.e: Councils running their own pounds had a euthanasia rate (~46%) nearly double that of welfare organizations (~25%).

mcqs.q: What was notable about reclaim rates across agencies?
o: They were low across all agencies
They were highest at rescue groups
mcqs.e: Reclaim rates were low across all of the agencies studied.

mcqs.q: Which virus was NOT inactivated by gaseous ozone even after 6 hours?
mcqs.e: Feline parvovirus (a non-enveloped virus) remained viable even after 6 hours of ozone.

mcqs.q: What general pattern of ozone susceptibility did the study confirm?
o: Enveloped viruses showed lower resistance to ozone
mcqs.e: Results confirmed lower resistance to ozone in enveloped viruses.

mcqs.q: After how long of ozone application did feline coronavirus show no cytopathic effect?
mcqs.e: Feline coronavirus showed no cytopathic effect after 2 hours of ozone application.

mcqs.q: What overall trend in public shelter intakes and outcomes occurred in Taiwan from 2012 to 2020?
mcqs.e: Shelter animal intakes and outcomes significantly decreased over the study period.

mcqs.q: What replaced euthanasia as the main reasons for animal outcomes?
mcqs.e: Adoption and trap–neuter–vaccination–return became the main reasons for animal outcomes.

mcqs.q: What happened to shelter veterinary workload relative to the legal limit (100 animals/vet)?
o: It stayed below the limit everywhere
It exceeded the limit in a growing number of counties
mcqs.e: Workload exceeded the legal limit in two counties in 2018, rising to six counties by 2020.

mcqs.q: What did this study conclude was most important to volunteer satisfaction?
o: Policies and procedures under organizational control
mcqs.e: Organizational policies and procedures were concluded to be most important to volunteer satisfaction.

mcqs.q: The study assessed the relative importance of which sets of factors?
o: Volunteer demographics, shelter attributes, and governing policies
mcqs.e: It compared volunteer demographics, shelter attributes, and the policies/procedures governing the experience.

mcqs.q: Which housing setting was associated with a higher frequency of sickness in cats?
mcqs.e: Cats in the cat café had a significantly higher frequency of sickness than foster-care cats.

mcqs.q: How did adoption speed compare by housing status?
mcqs.e: Foster-care cats were adopted significantly faster than cat café cats.

mcqs.q: What effect did negative behavioral and medical comments have on length of stay?
mcqs.e: Each additional negative behavioral or medical comment was associated with a longer length of stay.

mcqs.q: What did paired pre-/post-test scores show after the online asynchronous shelter surgery coursework?
o: A statistically significant increase in post-test scores
mcqs.e: Post-test scores increased significantly compared with pre-test scores (p < .001).

mcqs.q: Did time to completion (≤30 days vs >30 days) affect the change in scores?
o: No significant difference in mean score change
mcqs.e: There was no significant difference in score change between students finishing in 30 days or less versus more than 30 days.

mcqs.q: What did the findings support regarding instructional format?
o: Online asynchronous learning is an effective option
mcqs.e: The findings support online asynchronous learning as an effective option for veterinary students.
